newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah stable, call money fluctuates.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah stable, call money fluctuates.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah was stable against the dollar, but overnight money fluctuated in the afternoon on Wednesday, dealers said.

"As a whole it's quite a steady day despite brief rises in overnight money," one local bank dealer said. He said adequate rupiah supply and long period of preparation helped prevent wild swings on the first day of a new bank reserve requirement rate.
Banks have to comply with the new reserve requirement of five percent effective Wednesday, which dealers said would drain some five to eight trillion rupiah from the system.
He said overnight dollar rose briefly to a high of 7.75 percent but fell later back to 5.75 percent, suggesting overall that the market was stable.
One-week dollar was last given at 6.75 percent, down from an early level of 7.5 percent.
Another dealer said spot rupiah, due Monday, edged up briefly to 2,407.25 in response to the jump in overnight money before settling later at 2,407.50/07.75 at 0820 GMT.
Tomorrow and today rupiah closed at 2,406.15/06.65 and 2,406.5/07.0, respectively.
Overnight money, a measure of market readiness to cope with the new rate, was relatively stable throughout the morning, rising slightly to 13.5 percent from 11.0 percent.
"But the rate jumped shortly after the first clearing to a high of 20 percent although it could not hold for long," the local bank dealer said, adding it later fell to 10.0 percent.
"Some banks might have been caught short, forcing them to cover immediately as reflected by the sudden rise," he said.
One Japanese bank dealer said, howver, the market was well prepared to meet the two percentage point hike, thanks to an early announcement by the central bank.
Tom/next swap edged up to 1.5 before cooling down to 1.15/1.35 points. Overnight swap ended at 0.45/0.50.
Dealers said overall trading was lacklustre except for the brief jolt in the money market. Swap rates were also stable.
A long weekend premium was priced in the spot rate because the market will be closed on Friday for a public holiday.
The local bank dealer said operators would remain cautious on Thursday as operators adjusted to the new reserve rate.
"I think operators might prefer to be slightly long on dollars as the general election comes closer," he said.
"I don't think they would want to be caught short through the weekend if something happens," the dealer said.
One-month swaps were at 11.25/11.50, two at 23.5/24.5, three at 34.25/35.00 and six at 70.50/71.00 points.
Bank Indonesia kept its intervention band at 2,401/2,593 and the conversion band at 2,401/2,449 on Wednesday.
